newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico livestock, feed sectors ponder peso decline.
newsitem.headline: Mexico livestock, feed sectors ponder peso decline.

text.p: Mexican livestock producers and feed manufacturers are busy calculating the effects of a recent slide in grains and oilseed prices and also a recent weakening of the peso, sector sources said Monday.

"It is a win some/lose some situation that is causing both livestock producers and feed manufacturers to calculate where they stand in terms of price," said one source from the Association of Producers of Industrial Oils and Edible Fats.
Mexico's peso has dropped from around 7.5 to 7.95 pesos per dollar in the last four weeks, causing importers to pay out more for dollar-quoted commodities.
Grains and oilseeds have also generally moved lower in the same period, lessening the burden.
"The effect (of the peso fall) is that local meal is a much better deal than imported meal," the local office of the American Soybean Association (ASA) said in an update.
"Also, crushers are using up their inventories of high priced soybeans and will soon be processing the more recent lower priced beans," the ASA said.

"This should motivate tham to maintain peso prices of meal in the future if the peso does not slide any further. If the peso slides past the 8.10 (per dollar) mark, then crushers will pressure for a price increase in meal," it added.
Crushers, importing the vast majority of soybeans, have so far maintained their prices in pesos, the ASA said.
Livestock producers have been under pressure for months because of depressed end product prices in still-slack national demand.
The ASA reported the national average soybean meal price is around 2,500 pesos per tonne, with ranges between 2,400 and 2,640 pesos.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
